paragraphs.text: Rule definitions for linguistic review
Please review the linguistic accuracy of each definition. Traditional rules and AI evaluation rules are presented separately. The definitions retain their original wording.
Traditional rules
1  Aspect marker 了 for completed actions
Aspect marker 了 for completed actions / change of state -- when it must be added, and when it must NOT be added (e.g. habitual/routine actions take no 了).
2  Aspect marker 着 for durative actions
Aspect marker 着 marking an ongoing/durative action (e.g. two simultaneous actions, Place + V.着 + Obj.).
3  Aspect marker 过 for past experiences
Aspect marker 过 for a past experience; misused when the experience has not actually happened yet.
4  Directional complement
Directional complement word order: V. + directional complement (上/下/进/出) + Place + 来/去; 来/去 cannot directly take an object.
5  Ba construction
把-construction (disposal construction): used only for a deliberately initiated action on an object; typically ends with 了.
6  Bei passive
被-passive voice: marks something being done TO the subject; the following verb must fit an inanimate/passive-compatible sense.
7  Measure word
Measure word (MW) usage: num. + MW + noun; specific 的-marked nouns are usually not paired with 着-durative existential sentences.
8  Location zai place
在 + Place phrase required before a verb of location/position.
9  Preposition cong place
从 + Place ('from a place'); the object of 从 must be an actual place, not a person/abstract noun.
10  Preposition dao place
到 + Place ('to a place').
11  不是……而是…… construction
不是……而是…… ('not X but Y') used to refute a conventional assumption and assert the correct fact; subject placement rules.
12  Cai jiu construction
才 Num. 就 V. construction expressing 'only/as early as Num., already V.'
13  Laoshi negative connotation
老是 ('always/keeps on') carries a negative, complaining connotation -- wrong when the sentence is neutral/positive.
14  Gen he accompanying zhe
跟/和 + noun requires both nouns to perform the SAME action independently; when one entity is led/carried by another, use V.着 (e.g. 牵着驴) instead.
15  Jieguo unexpected result
结果 introduces an unexpected result, not a plain sequential outcome.
16  又 and 也 distinction
又 (repetition of a prior action) vs. 也 (similarity to another party's action).
17  Haide harmful result
害得 must be followed by a clearly harmful/negative consequence, not a neutral one.
18  Wrong character
错别字 -- a wrong/miswritten Chinese character (as opposed to a word-choice/vocabulary problem).
19  Redundancy delete
Redundant word/phrase that should simply be deleted (repeated subject, repeated adverb, etc.).
20  Ambiguous reference
Ambiguous or vague referent (pronoun 他/她 unclear, vague noun like 人/事情/别人 needing specificity).
21  Character introduction first mention
A character should be briefly introduced on first mention (name + who they are) rather than assumed known.
22  Coherence connectives
Discourse coherence: sentences are loosely strung together without connectives/transitions.
23  Modal verb no le
Modal verbs (叫/让/想/要 etc.) are not followed by aspect marker 了.
24  Verb reduplication
Verb reduplication (V.V., e.g. 玩玩, 想想) used for light/tentative requests or plans.
25  Adverbial de multisyllabic
地-marked adverbials: only multi-syllabic (2+ character) adverbs take 地 before a verb; monosyllabic adverbs do not.
26  Resultative complement
Resultative complement (V. + result, e.g. 擦干净, 写下, 吃到): the action verb alone vs. action + result -- 看 look vs. 看到 see, 找 look for vs. 找到 find, 听 vs. 听到, 注意 vs. 注意到.
27  Topic comment missing subject
Topic-comment sentences may legitimately omit an already-clear subject; not every omission is an error.
28  Repeated wh whichever
Repeated wh-word construction ('哪一X就V哪一X') expressing 'whichever..., that one...'
29  Comparative sentence
Comparative sentence structures (比, 都, 最...不过了) and words that cannot be used inside a comparison.
30  Num mw noun no de
Num. + MW. + noun does not take 的 (e.g. 一筐梨, not 一筐的梨).
31  Verb object collocation

Collocation/valence errors: the verb cannot take that object or complement (想 + V. not N., 想让 Sb. V., 成为 + N.), an adjective does not go with that noun (良好 + 生活), or a verb conflicts with an adjacent verb.
32  Wrong information content
Factual/content error: the sentence states something that contradicts the story's actual plot.
33  Aspect zai progressive
在/正在 + V. marks an ongoing action (一直在学习); do not add 在 when the action is not ongoing.
34  Potential complement
Potential complement V.得/不 + result (睡不好, 想得起来) for whether an outcome can be achieved.
35  Degree complement de
Degree complement V.得 + Adj. (病得很重, 搬得太频繁) rather than putting the degree word directly after the verb; 病/生病 cannot take 很 directly.
36  不是……就是…… construction
不是……就是…… means 'either ... or ...' (two alternatives that both happen); it is not 'not X but Y' (that is 不是……而是……). The subject goes before 不是.
37  这就要看……了 construction
这就要看……了 ('it depends on ...'): needs an uncertain condition before it (e.g. 会不会生病？) and an A-not-A / open question after 看.
38  Example marker tebie bifang
特别是 + N./clause singles out a typical example of what was just said; 比方说 introduces an example. Neither can replace 特别 (very) or stand without the general statement.
39  A not A questions
Embedded yes/no questions use A-not-A (有没有毒, 能不能吃, 知不知道) or 是……还是……; 'whether/if' in 'know if' is not 如果.
40  Adjective predicate
Adjectives are predicates on their own and normally take 很 (or another degree adverb) without 是 (他很聪明, not 他是聪明); 是……的 only for emphasis.
41  都 and totality
都 is required after totality expressions (从早到晚都, 每天都, 每人都, 什么都) and with 一直/也 in such sentences.
42  和 connects nouns only
和 links nouns/noun phrases only; it cannot link verb phrases, adjectives, or clauses (use 也, 又……又……, 而且, or a comma).
43  Attributive modifier de
Modifiers come before the noun with 的 (一个叫孟子的小孩子, 住在离墓地很近的地方, 有毒的植物); no 的 after 很多 or in fixed phrases (好主意).
44  Adverbial word order
Word order: subject first, then time/frequency/manner adverbials (常常, 都, 也, 先, 一共), then place (在 + Place), then the verb; duration and frequency after the verb (住了一个星期).
45  Time expression
Time expressions: 在古代 (not 古代的时候), 后来 vs. 以后 vs. 将来, 长大以后, Time + 以后; 'then' in a narrative is 然后/后来, not 以后 alone.
46  Missing subject
A required subject is missing (or must be restated after an aside), so the reader cannot tell who acts.
47  Reference form

Choosing the referring form: use a pronoun or zero form when the referent is clear instead of repeating the name, restore the name when the pronoun is ambiguous, and use 我/我们/你们 correctly inside quoted speech.
48  Word choice
Wrong or less suitable word: near-synonyms (别的 vs. 另外, 高兴 vs. 幸福, 食品 vs. 食物, 将来 vs. 后来), register, and words whose meaning does not fit the context.
49  Word class misuse
A word used in the wrong part of speech: a noun used as a verb or adjective (经验, 毒 -> 有毒), an adjective used as a verb (合适 vs. 适合), 病 as a gradable adjective.
50  又 and 再 distinction
又 for a repeated action that already happened (又搬家了) vs. 再 for one that has not happened yet (要再搬一次家).
51  Sentence restructure
The sentence needs rewriting as a whole; the teacher gives a reformulation rather than a single rule. (Not built into a rule card.)

AI evaluation rules
1  Missed error
AI failed to catch an error the teacher flagged (issue #1: AI often misses needed corrections).
2  Incorrect correction
AI's proposed correction is itself linguistically wrong (issue #2a: sometimes AI 'fixes' a correct original into something wrong).
3  Correct fix wrong or missing explanation
AI's corrected text happens to be right, but the grammatical explanation is wrong or absent (issue #2b).
4  False positive unneeded correction
AI flagged/changed something that was already correct and needed no revision (issue #1/#3, over-correction).
5  Disfluency false positive
AI's feedback targets a spoken-transcript disfluency (repetition/pause/filler) that should simply be removed in cleanup, not treated as a grammar error.
6  Misleading no error framing
AI says 'no correction needed' but still narrates a 'rule violated', which is self-contradictory and misleading (issue #3).
7  Misdirected feedback
AI labels span A as incorrect but the explanation/fix actually concerns a different span B (issue #4).
8  Miscategorized error type
AI filed the issue under the wrong category, e.g. a vocabulary problem listed as grammar, or a vocabulary-misuse case labeled 错别字 (issue #5).
9  Grammatical but semantically off
AI's fix is grammatically valid but semantically/pragmatically wrong given the story context.
10  Disputed rule claim
Teacher disputes the existence/applicability of the grammar rule AI invoked.
11  Validated correct
Teacher confirms this AI feedback item is fully correct (both fix and explanation) -- a positive calibration example.
12  Inappropriate vocab alternative

AI's vocabulary suggestion offers an alternative that is wrong, too strong, too literary, or awkward in context (e.g. 饿叫, 携走, 低贱/卑微, 不良分子) -- every suggested alternative must itself be correct and natural at the student's level.
13  Unclassified
Teacher's comment did not match a known pattern; needs manual review.

comments.author: Shuyi Yang
comments.text: If the focus is not “completion or not”, do not use 了. Also mental state verbs do not take 了 (e.g., 觉得，知道，认为，决定). The speaking words that introduce quoted speech do not take 了.

comments.author: Shuyi Yang
comments.text: Durative state: not very “active” action, but relatively “static” state; not for two simultaneous actions (which is 一边……一边……), but for accompanying state/action (not the main action). 着 is used for "background" (not the foreground/focus).

anchor.text: an ongoing/durative action (e.g. two simultaneous actions

comments.author: Shuyi Yang
comments.text: And this experience has impact upon the present: there is often a follow-up statement, resulting from the experience. Usually not for routine/everyday activities such as eating, sleeping, drinking, etc.

comments.author: Shuyi Yang
comments.text: It depends. When the Obj. is an item (not a place), 来/去 can take it: V. + directional complement + 来/去 + Obj. (e.g., 拿出来一个梨，放上去一筐梨), or V. + directional complement + 来/去 + Obj. (e.g., 拿出一个梨来). When the Obj. is a place, 来/去 cannot directly take it.

anchor.text: 来/去 cannot directly take an object

comments.author: Shuyi Yang
comments.text: More accurate: Subj. does something to Obj., causing Obj. to change. The verb must refer to actions that can cause changes. When Obj.’s location is changed because Subj.’s action, 把 must be used (when there is a place, an obj. and a change of location).

anchor.text: used only for a deliberately initiated action on an object

comments.author: Shuyi Yang
comments.text: Not necessarily “inanimate” verbs, e.g., 被打了，打 is not inanimate. In 被: the “Subj.” is the recipient of the action, not the performer. Usually with a negative connotation: something bad is done to the subj.

anchor.text: the following verb must fit an inanimate/passive-compatible sense

comments.author: Shuyi Yang
comments.text: A bit confusing about “specific 的 marked nouns". I understand that 着 existential sentence “there be” usually did not take the definite Obj. (e.g., we do not say: there is “put” that shirt.), but rather a generic Obj. (usually num. MW. Noun)

anchor.text: specific 的-marked nouns are usually not paired with 着-durative existential sentences

comments.author: Shuyi Yang
comments.text: If the obj. is a person/abstract noun, usually need place marker like “那儿" or “中" attached, e.g., 从王朋那儿来，从经验中得到……

comments.author: Shuyi Yang
comments.text: I do not fully understand “subject placement rules”.

comments.author: Shuyi Yang
comments.text: Early/small amount, e.g., 才吃了两口饭就饱了

comments.author: Shuyi Yang
comments.text: Correct, and usually a bad result

comments.author: Shuyi Yang
comments.text: 害得 must be followed by the recipient of the harmful consequence. The structure is: ……害得someone + VP/clause

comments.author: Shuyi Yang
comments.text: More modal verb examples: 会/能/需要/得/可以/不准

comments.author: Shuyi Yang [2]
comments.text: And also “V一V”

comments.author: Shuyi Yang
comments.text: Many verbs in Chinese are procedure/attempt verbs, only denoting the action, not the result. When result is included, resultative complement should be added.

comments.author: Shuyi Yang
comments.text: This is more about a topic-chain: if a series of run-on sentences share the same topic, the later sentences can and should omit the shared topic.

anchor.text: may legitimately omit an already-clear subject

comments.author: Shuyi Yang
comments.text: The position of the later repeated “wh-word” depends on its role: if it is “whenever”, 什么时候……，就什么时候……. If it is “wherever” and it serves as Subj., 哪儿……，哪儿就……, if it serves as Obj., 哪儿……，就V哪儿. If it is “whatever/whichever/whoever” and it serves as Subj., 什么/哪MW./谁……，什么/哪MW./谁就……, if it serves as Obj., 什么/哪MW./谁……，就V什么/哪MW./谁. If it is “however”, 怎么V.……，就怎么V.

comments.author: Shuyi Yang
comments.text: Comparative sentence structure is A比B……. “都" is both/all, which is not comparative sentence structure. “最……不过了" is not a comparative structure; it expresses “the best option”, and only a few adjectives can enter, e.g., 好/合适/理想.

anchor.text: Comparative sentence structures (比, 都, 最...不过了) and words that cannot be used inside a comparison.

comments.author: Shuyi Yang
comments.text: 在/正在 is for "foreground/focus", in contrast to 着, which is for “background” (durative, accompanying/static).

comments.author: Shuyi Yang
comments.text: Correct, and it is about the (in)ability, (im)possibility

comments.author: Shuyi Yang
comments.text: I assume here it means for some adjectives (e.g., 病), they refer to states that do not have “degrees” (one is either sick or not sick), we do not put degree words (e.g., 很，太，有点儿) before it, it is wrong to say 很病. But rather we use “degree/descriptive complement得", 病得很重

comments.text: Correct: 这就要看……了 is a flexible response to a question/uncertain condition, instead of giving a direct answer, 这就要看……了 gives a flexible response "depending on…". The structure after 看 should be a question form, A-not-A/wh-word/A还是B
